first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and simplifying onboarding has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This directly addresses two observed leading indicators of sustainable qualified revenue. Verify the onboarding result and the competing pricing evidence because competitor pricing makes the opportunity cost of this choice consequential; run a controlled standard experiment rather than assume the historical effect transfers unchanged.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-shortening experiment. The verified prior result directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and supports sustainable value: completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. This is better aligned to long-term qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose verified result showed a 12% 30-day-retention decline despite short-term revenue lift. Monitor qualification, retained qualified revenue, and downstream activation so reduced onboarding steps do not lower account quality or required-data capture.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-shortening experiment. The verified evidence supports sustainable improvement in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while the only directly relevant pricing evidence shows targeted discounts produce acquisition gains but materially weaker retention. The competitor's deeper cut increases urgency, but it does not establish that matching price will retain qualified SMB accounts or create durable revenue. Track SMB qualification, activation, retained qualified revenue, and churn by price sensitivity; address immediate churn conversations through non-experiment customer-success handling rather than consuming the experiment slot on an unproven retention discount.
